title: When a node re-runs: fingerprints, the NaN trick, not_idempotent
hook: float("NaN") makes a node run every time, and math.nan doesn't. Three hooks decide if your node runs and if your graph is allowed to start.

verified.claim: Over 3 queues: no hook 1 run, False 1, None 1, fixed dict 1, fixed list 1, new float('NaN') 3, math.nan 1, one module-level NaN 1, a rising counter 3, a tensor 3, a hook that raises 3.
verified.ref: test nodes through one PromptExecutor with the classic cache, CPU

verified.claim: A NaN from a V3 fingerprint_inputs also re-ran on every queue, and everything downstream ran too.
A fingerprint sees constants only: a wired input arrived as None.
verified.ref: execution.py:IsChangedCache calls get_input_data with no execution list

verified.claim: A hook that raises sets the key to NaN and logs a warning.
Two copies of an ordinary node with the same inputs ran once. With not_idempotent they ran twice, then not at all on the next queue.
Naming an input in validate_inputs turned off its range check, and left the others on. Using input_types turned off the type check.
A validator that returns False gives custom_validation_failed, one error per input it received. One that raises gives exception_during_validation.

unchecked: Our explanation of why math.nan fails is Python's rule that containers compare identical objects as equal. The counts are measured. We didn't step through to_hashable to watch it happen.
Exact counts for not_idempotent across other cache modes. We used the classic cache.
